items.question: What is the maximum total number of occupants, including crew, in high-density configuration?
items.explanation: In high-density cabin configuration the total number of occupants, including crew, shall not exceed 17.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the maximum total number of occupants, including crew, in low-density configuration?
items.explanation: In low-density cabin configuration the total number of occupants, including crew, shall not exceed 14.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the minimum number of passenger seats that must remain installed in the cabin?
options: 3 seats in at least one row
items.explanation: The RFM requires that a minimum of 3 seats in at least one row remain installed in the cabin.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: Under day VFR according to the basic RFM, what is the minimum flight crew requirement?
options: One pilot, single-pilot operation not permitted from left seat
Two pilots, one in each front seat
One pilot from either left or right seat
One pilot plus one flight engineer
items.explanation: For day VFR the minimum flight crew is one pilot, and single-pilot operation is not permitted from the left seat.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight for towing or taxi?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight for towing or taxi is 6450 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight for CAT B take-off and landing?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight for Category B take-off and landing is 6400 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the minimum flight/rotor running gross weight?
items.explanation: Minimum flight/rotor running gross weight is 4400 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed when operating with Take-Off Power?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed with Take-Off Power applied is 90 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed when main rotor speed NR is at 102%?
items.explanation: With NR at 102% the maximum airspeed is limited to 90 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Minimum airspeed for flight under IFR (Vmini) is?
items.explanation: Vmini for IFR operations is 50 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for IFR approach?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for IFR approach is 150 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Maximum airspeed for climb with one autopilot (AP) failed is?
items.explanation: With one AP failed the maximum airspeed for climb is 100 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Maximum rate of climb with one autopilot (AP) failed is?
items.explanation: With one AP failed, the maximum permitted rate of climb is 1000 fpm.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed with one autopilot (AP) failed?
items.explanation: With one AP failed the maximum airspeed is limited to Vne - 27 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for landing gear operation and with landing gear extended (Vlo/Vle)?
items.explanation: Both maximum landing gear operating speed (Vlo) and gear extended speed (Vle) are 150 KIAS or Vne if less.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Minimum airspeed in autorotation is?
items.explanation: The minimum airspeed in autorotation is 40 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Maximum airspeed with the right cabin door locked open is?
items.explanation: With the right cabin door locked open maximum airspeed is 100 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Maximum airspeed with the left or both cabin doors locked open is?
items.explanation: With the left or both cabin doors locked open maximum airspeed is 80 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Maximum airspeed for opening or closing the cabin doors is?
items.explanation: Opening or closing the cabin doors is limited to 80 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Maximum airspeed for operation of the windscreen wipers is?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for operation of windscreen wipers is 140 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: On paved surfaces, what is the maximum taxi speed?
items.explanation: Maximum taxi speed on paved surfaces is 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On paved surfaces, what is the maximum speed for emergency landing (nose wheel locked fore and aft)?
items.explanation: Maximum speed for emergency landing on paved surfaces is 60 knots (110 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: What is the maximum towing speed on paved surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum towing speed on paved surfaces is 37 km/hr (23 mph).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On prepared grass surfaces, what is the maximum taxi speed?
items.explanation: On prepared grass, maximum taxi speed is 20 knots (37 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On prepared grass surfaces, what is the maximum speed for emergency landing?
items.explanation: On prepared grass, maximum speed for emergency landing is 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: What is the maximum wind speed for rotor starting and stopping?
items.explanation: Maximum wind speed for rotor starting and stopping is 60 knots (30 m/s).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WIND SPEED LIMITATIONS FOR ROTOR STARTING AND STOPPING (p.1-8)

items.question: When rotor starting/stopping with winds above 33 knots (17 m/s), what must be recorded?
options: Actual windspeed in the helicopter log book
items.explanation: For rotor starting and stopping with windspeeds above 33 knots, the actual windspeed must be recorded in the helicopter log book.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WIND SPEED LIMITATIONS FOR ROTOR STARTING AND STOPPING (p.1-8)

items.question: What is the minimum outside air temperature (OAT) for ground starting?
items.explanation: Minimum ambient air temperature for ground starting is -40 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AMBIENT AIR TEMPERATURE LIMITATIONS (OAT)

items.question: According to the basic RFM, is flight into known icing conditions permitted?
options: Only with ice protection systems ON
items.explanation: The basic AW139 RFM states that flight into known icing conditions is prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ICING LIMITATIONS

items.question: According to the basic RFM, is flight into freezing rain permitted?
options: No, flight into freezing rain is prohibited
items.explanation: The basic RFM explicitly prohibits flight into freezing rain.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ICING LIMITATIONS

items.question: Are aerobatic manoeuvres permitted?
items.explanation: Section 1 MANOEUVRING LIMITATIONS states that aerobatic manoeuvres are prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MANOEUVRING LIMITATIONS (p.1-19)

items.question: Are practice autorotative landings permitted?
options: Yes, but only on paved surfaces
No, practice autorotative landings are prohibited
items.explanation: AUTOROTATION LIMITATIONS state that practice autorotative landings are prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AUTOROTATION LIMITATIONS (p.1-19)

items.question: During autorotation, when may the ENG MODE select switch be retarded from FLIGHT to IDLE?
options: Only when both engines are failed
items.explanation: The RFM states that during autorotation the ENG MODE select switch must not be retarded from FLIGHT to IDLE except in an emergency.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AUTOROTATION LIMITATIONS (p.1-19)

items.question: What are the basic RFM slope limitations for sloped take-off and landing?
items.explanation: In the basic RFM, sloped take-off and landing are limited to 5 deg nose up, 5 deg nose down, 5 deg left wing low and 5 deg right wing low.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: SLOPE LIMITATIONS (p.1-19)

items.question: What is the maximum running speed for wheel brake application?
items.explanation: Wheel brake limitations specify a maximum running speed for brake application of 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WHEEL BRAKE LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: How long is parking on slopes up to 10 deg permitted?
items.explanation: Parking on slopes up to 10 deg is permitted for a maximum of 1 hour.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WHEEL BRAKE LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: At what indicated OAT must pitot heating be switched ON?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be switched ON for indicated outside air temperature of +4 deg C or less.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: PITOT HEATING LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: At what indicated OAT must pitot heating be switched OFF?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be switched OFF at indicated outside air temperature of +10 deg C or more.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: PITOT HEATING LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: What is the total usable fuel capacity?
items.explanation: Total usable fuel capacity is 1588 litres.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FUEL CAPACITIES (p.1-28)

items.question: What is the unusable fuel quantity?
items.explanation: Unusable fuel quantity is 20 litres.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FUEL CAPACITIES (p.1-28)

items.question: In coordinated flight, what unusable fuel is indicated and what is the actual per tank?
options: 0 kg indicated / 5 kg per tank actual
0 kg indicated / 8 kg (10 litres) per tank actual
5 kg indicated / 8 kg per tank actual
8 kg indicated / 10 kg per tank actual
items.explanation: In coordinated flight the indication is 0 kg unusable, which corresponds to 8 kg/10 litres per tank actual.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: UNUSABLE FUEL (p.1-28)

items.question: When is hovering in crosswinds or sideways flight with sustained roll angles greater than 15 deg prohibited?
options: When either tank indicates less than 50 kg
When either tank indicates less than 60 kg
When either tank indicates less than 70 kg
When total fuel is less than 140 kg
items.explanation: Hovering in crosswinds or sideways flight with sustained roll angles greater than 15 deg is prohibited when fuel indication in either tank is less than 70 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: UNUSABLE FUEL (p.1-28)

items.question: What is the maximum crossfeeding amount (tank with pump off, not supplying engines)?
items.explanation: Maximum crossfeeding amount is 228 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: UNUSABLE FUEL (p.1-28)

items.question: What is the fuel pressure cautionary range?
items.explanation: Fuel pressure cautionary range is 0.0 to 0.5 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FUEL PRESSURE (BAR) (p.1-28)

items.question: What is the minimum fuel pressure for normal operation?
items.explanation: Minimum fuel pressure for normal operation is 0.6 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FUEL PRESSURE (BAR) (p.1-28)

items.question: What is the normal fuel pressure operation range?
items.explanation: Normal fuel pressure operation range is 0.6 to 2.1 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FUEL PRESSURE (BAR) (p.1-28)

items.question: What is the maximum fuel pressure?
items.explanation: Maximum fuel pressure is 2.1 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FUEL PRESSURE (BAR) (p.1-28)

items.question: What is the minimum engine oil pressure for normal operation?
items.explanation: Figure 1-27 shows minimum engine oil pressure for normal operation as 6.3 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: Engine Oil Pressure (Figure 1-27, p.1-55)

items.question: What is the maximum engine oil pressure for normal operation?
items.explanation: Figure 1-27 shows maximum engine oil pressure for normal operation as 8.9 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: Engine Oil Pressure (Figure 1-27, p.1-55)

items.question: What is the minimum engine oil pressure allowed at ground idle (GI) for up to 1 minute?
items.explanation: Figure 1-27 specifies a minimum engine oil pressure at ground idle (GI) of 4.2 bar for up to 1 minute.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: Engine Oil Pressure (Figure 1-27, p.1-55)

items.question: How many occupants including crew may be carried in high-density configuration without exceeding the limitation?
items.explanation: In high-density configuration the total number of occupants including crew must not exceed 17.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: A high-density cabin manifest shows 18 occupants including crew. How does this compare to the limitation?
items.explanation: The high-density limit is 17 occupants including crew, so 18 would exceed the limit by 1.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the maximum total number of occupants including crew in low-density configuration?
items.explanation: In low-density configuration the total number of occupants including crew must not exceed 14.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: In low-density configuration, planning 15 occupants including crew is:
items.explanation: The low-density limitation is 14 occupants including crew, so 15 would be above the limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: Which cabin configuration statement is correct according to the AW139 RFM?
items.explanation: The RFM states a maximum of 17 occupants in high-density and 14 in low-density configuration.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the minimum number of seats that must remain installed in at least one cabin row?
items.explanation: A minimum of 3 seats must remain installed in at least one cabin row.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: If only two seats remain installed in a single row, this is:
options: Acceptable if weight and balance are within limits
Not permitted because at least 3 seats must remain in one row
items.explanation: The RFM requires at least 3 seats to remain installed in at least one row, so only two in any row would not meet the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: For day VFR operations under the basic RFM, what is the minimum required flight crew?
options: One pilot and one technical crew member
items.explanation: The basic RFM states the minimum flight crew for day VFR is one pilot.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW (p.1-1)

items.question: Under the basic RFM, where is single-pilot operation not permitted from?
items.explanation: Single-pilot operation is not permitted from the left seat according to the basic RFM.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW (p.1-1)

items.question: A single pilot intends to fly day VFR from the left seat. This is:
items.explanation: The basic RFM does not permit single-pilot operation from the left seat.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight permitted for towing or taxiing the helicopter?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight for towing or taxi is 6450 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: A dispatch weight of 6500 kg is planned for taxi. How does this compare with the towing/taxi limitation?
items.explanation: Taxi and towing are limited to 6450 kg, so 6500 kg would exceed the limitation by 50 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight for Category B take-off and landing?
items.explanation: Category B take-off and landing are limited to a maximum gross weight of 6400 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: A planned Category B landing weight of 6450 kg is:
options: Within the Category B landing limit
At the Category B landing limit
Above the Category B landing limit
items.explanation: The Category B take-off and landing limit is 6400 kg, so 6450 kg would be above the limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the minimum gross weight permitted for flight or rotor running?
items.explanation: Minimum flight or rotor running gross weight is 4400 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: Dispatching with a planned take-off weight of 4300 kg is:
options: Below the minimum flight gross weight
At the minimum flight gross weight
Above the minimum flight gross weight
Not affected by minimum weight limits
items.explanation: The minimum flight gross weight is 4400 kg, so 4300 kg would be below the minimum.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed allowed when Take-Off Power is being used?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed with Take-Off Power applied is 90 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: A pilot intends to maintain 95 KIAS with Take-Off Power applied. This is:
options: Within the Take-Off Power airspeed limit
Above the Take-Off Power airspeed limit
items.explanation: The Take-Off Power airspeed limit is 90 KIAS, so 95 KIAS would exceed the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: With main rotor speed NR at 102 percent, what is the associated maximum airspeed?
items.explanation: At NR 102 percent, maximum airspeed is limited to 90 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Flying at 100 KIAS with NR at 102 percent is:
options: Exceeding the NR 102 percent airspeed limit
Only allowed with both APs engaged
items.explanation: With NR at 102 percent, airspeed must not exceed 90 KIAS, so 100 KIAS would exceed the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the minimum airspeed for IFR flight (Vmini) according to the AW139 RFM?
items.explanation: The minimum airspeed for IFR flight, Vmini, is 50 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: An IFR departure is flown at 45 KIAS. This airspeed is:
options: Only permitted with one AP failed
items.explanation: Vmini for IFR is 50 KIAS, so 45 KIAS is below the minimum IFR airspeed.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for IFR approach?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for IFR approach is 150 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: During an IFR approach, flying at 155 KIAS is:
options: Only permitted with both APs engaged
items.explanation: The IFR approach limit is 150 KIAS, so 155 KIAS would be above the permitted airspeed.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: With one autopilot failed, what is the maximum airspeed for climb?
items.explanation: With one AP failed, maximum airspeed for climb is 100 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: A climb is flown at 110 KIAS with one autopilot failed. This is:
items.explanation: When one AP is failed, climb airspeed is limited to 100 KIAS, so 110 KIAS exceeds this limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: With one autopilot failed, what is the maximum permitted rate of climb?
items.explanation: Maximum rate of climb with one AP failed is 1000 fpm.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: A climb is flown at 1200 fpm with one AP failed. How does this compare to the limitation?
items.explanation: The limit is 1000 fpm with one AP failed, so 1200 fpm exceeds the permitted rate of climb by 200 fpm.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: With one autopilot failed, the maximum airspeed is limited to:
items.explanation: The RFM limits maximum airspeed with one AP failed to Vne - 27 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Which statement about one-autopilot-failed airspeed limitations is correct?
options: There is no airspeed reduction with one AP failed
Maximum airspeed is reduced to Vne - 27 KIAS
Maximum airspeed is reduced to Vne - 10 KIAS
Maximum airspeed is limited to 90 KIAS
items.explanation: With one AP failed, the maximum airspeed is Vne - 27 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for landing gear operation and with landing gear extended (Vlo/Vle)?
items.explanation: Both Vlo and Vle are 150 KIAS or Vne if less.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Operating the landing gear at 160 KIAS is:
items.explanation: Vlo and Vle are 150 KIAS or Vne if less, so 160 KIAS is above the gear operation and extended speed limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the minimum airspeed in autorotation?
items.explanation: The minimum airspeed in autorotation is 40 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: During autorotation the pilot stabilises at 35 KIAS. This is:
options: Exactly at the minimum autorotation speed
Only a recommendation, not a limitation
items.explanation: The minimum airspeed in autorotation is 40 KIAS, so 35 KIAS is below the stated minimum.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed with the right cabin door locked open?
items.explanation: With the right cabin door locked open, maximum airspeed is 100 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Flying at 110 KIAS with the right cabin door locked open is:
items.explanation: The right cabin door locked open limit is 100 KIAS, so 110 KIAS exceeds the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed with the left or both cabin doors locked open?
items.explanation: With the left or both cabin doors locked open, maximum airspeed is 80 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: With both cabin doors locked open, flying at 90 KIAS is:
items.explanation: The limit with left or both doors locked open is 80 KIAS, so 90 KIAS exceeds the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for opening or closing the cabin doors?
items.explanation: Opening or closing the cabin doors is limited to 80 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Opening a cabin door at 90 KIAS is:
items.explanation: Door opening and closing is limited to 80 KIAS, so 90 KIAS is above the allowed speed.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for operation of the windscreen wipers?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for wiper operation is 140 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: Using the windscreen wipers at 150 KIAS is:
items.explanation: Wiper operation is limited to 140 KIAS, so 150 KIAS exceeds the limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AIRSPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: On paved surfaces, what is the maximum taxi speed?
items.explanation: Maximum taxi speed on paved surfaces is 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: Taxiing at 45 knots on a paved surface is:
items.explanation: Taxi speed on paved surfaces is limited to 40 knots, so 45 knots is above the limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On paved surfaces, what is the maximum speed for emergency landing with the nose wheel locked fore and aft?
items.explanation: Maximum emergency landing speed on paved surfaces is 60 knots (110 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: An emergency landing is conducted at 70 knots on a paved runway. This is:
items.explanation: Emergency landing speed on paved surfaces is limited to 60 knots, so 70 knots exceeds the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: What is the maximum towing speed on paved surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum towing speed on paved surfaces is 37 km/hr (23 mph).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: Towing the helicopter at 45 km/hr on paved surfaces is:
items.explanation: The towing speed limit on paved surfaces is 37 km/hr, so 45 km/hr exceeds the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On prepared grass surfaces, what is the maximum taxi speed?
items.explanation: On prepared grass, maximum taxi speed is 20 knots (37 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: Taxiing at 25 knots on prepared grass is:
options: Within the grass taxi speed limit
Above the grass taxi speed limit
items.explanation: Taxi speed on prepared grass is limited to 20 knots, so 25 knots exceeds the permitted taxi speed.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On prepared grass surfaces, what is the maximum speed for emergency landing?
items.explanation: On prepared grass, maximum emergency landing speed is 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: An emergency landing is carried out at 45 knots on prepared grass. This is:
items.explanation: Emergency landing speed on prepared grass is limited to 40 knots, so 45 knots is above the limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: With all engines operating, what is the minimum continuous rotor speed (NR)?
items.explanation: For power-on operation with all engines operating, minimum continuous NR is 98%; values between 95% and 98% are only permitted as brief transients.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)
NR limits table

items.question: With all engines operating, which NR range is approved for continuous operation?
items.explanation: Continuous power-on operation with all engines operating is approved between 98% and 101% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: During cruise with all engines operating, NR is stabilized at 101%. This is:
items.explanation: For all engines operating, continuous NR is allowed from 98% up to a maximum of 101% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: With all engines operating, NR peaks at 104% for 3 seconds during a maneuver. This is:
options: Above the maximum cautionary NR limit
items.explanation: For all engines operating, the cautionary NR range ends at 103% NR; 104% exceeds the maximum cautionary NR limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: With all engines operating, NR briefly reaches 106% for 5 seconds. This is:
items.explanation: With all engines operating, NR up to 106% is permitted as a transient condition for a maximum of 10 seconds.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)
NR transient limits

items.question: With all engines operating, NR is held at 106% for 20 seconds during a climb. This is:
items.explanation: NR 106% is only permitted as a 10-second transient; maintaining 106% NR for 20 seconds exceeds the transient time limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: For all engines operating, what is the rotor speed cautionary range?
items.explanation: With all engines operating, the cautionary rotor speed range is 101% to 103% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: For all engines operating, what is the maximum cautionary rotor speed (NR)?
items.explanation: For power-on operation with all engines operating, the cautionary NR range extends up to a maximum of 103% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: In cruise with all engines operating, NR is stabilized at 96%. This is:
options: Below the continuous NR range and only permitted transiently
Unrestricted for all phases of flight
items.explanation: Continuous AEO operation must remain between 98% and 101% NR; 96% NR is below the continuous range and only acceptable as a brief transient.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: With all engines operating, NR momentarily drops to 95% during a control input and recovers immediately. This is:
options: Within the permitted transient NR range
items.explanation: For AEO power-on operation, 95% NR is the minimum transient limit and is only permitted for short durations.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On AEO)

items.question: For one engine inoperative (OEI) operation, what is the minimum transient rotor speed (NR)?
items.explanation: With one engine inoperative, the minimum transient NR is 85%; operation below this value is not permitted.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)
OEI NR limits

items.question: For OEI landing only, what is the approved NR cautionary range?
items.explanation: With one engine inoperative, NR between 90% and 97% is a cautionary range approved for landing only.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: With one engine inoperative, what is the minimum continuous NR for power-on operation?
items.explanation: For OEI operation, minimum continuous rotor speed is 98% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: During an OEI approach, NR is stabilized at 97%. This is:
options: Within the OEI landing-only cautionary range
items.explanation: With one engine inoperative, 97% NR lies in the 90% to 97% cautionary range, which is approved for landing only, not for general continuous flight.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: During OEI operation, NR briefly drops to 89% before recovery. This is:
options: Below the cautionary range but within transient limits
items.explanation: For OEI, the cautionary range starts at 90% NR; 89% is below this but still above the minimum transient limit of 85% NR, so it is only acceptable as a brief transient.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: In OEI operation, NR is maintained at 100% during climb. This is:
options: Within the OEI continuous NR range
Below the OEI continuous NR range
Within the OEI transient range only
Above the OEI continuous NR range
items.explanation: For one engine inoperative, continuous NR operation is allowed between 98% and 101% NR, so 100% NR is within the continuous range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: During OEI climb, NR peaks at 103% for a few seconds. This is:
options: Within the OEI continuous NR range
Above the maximum cautionary NR limit
items.explanation: For OEI operation, a 101% to 103% NR range is cautionary; 103% is the upper limit of this cautionary range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: During OEI go-around, NR reaches 106% for 8 seconds. This is:
options: Within the OEI continuous NR range
Within the OEI 10-second transient NR limit
Above the OEI transient NR limit
Only allowed with both engines operating
items.explanation: For OEI, NR up to 106% is permitted as a transient condition for a maximum of 10 seconds; 8 seconds remains within this limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)
NR transient limits

items.question: During OEI climb, NR is held at 106% for 20 seconds. This is:
items.explanation: NR 106% is allowed only as a 10-second transient; 20 seconds exceeds the permitted transient duration.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: For OEI operation, what NR range is approved for continuous flight?
items.explanation: For one engine inoperative, continuous NR operation is approved from 98% to 101% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-On OEI)

items.question: In power-off (autorotation) flight, what is the minimum continuous rotor speed (NR)?
items.explanation: For power-off operation, minimum continuous NR is 95%; lower NR values are permitted only as brief transients.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)
Autorotation NR limits

items.question: In autorotation, which NR range is approved for continuous operation?
items.explanation: During power-off flight, continuous NR operation is approved between 95% and 110% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)

items.question: During autorotation, NR stabilizes at 93%. This is:
options: Below the continuous range and only permitted transiently
items.explanation: For power-off flight, continuous operation must remain at or above 95% NR; 93% NR is below the continuous range and only acceptable as a brief transient down to 90% NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)

items.question: During autorotation, NR reaches 112% for a few seconds before being corrected. This is:
options: Above the maximum transient NR limit
items.explanation: For power-off flight, the maximum continuous NR is 110%, and a transient up to 116% NR is permitted for a short duration; 112% falls within this transient range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)

items.question: During autorotation, NR peaks at 116% and is immediately reduced. This is:
options: Within the maximum transient NR limit
Above the maximum transient NR limit
items.explanation: In power-off flight, 116% NR is the upper limit of the transient range and must be corrected immediately.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)

items.question: During autorotation, NR increases to 118% before recovery. This is:
options: Above the maximum transient NR limit
items.explanation: For power-off flight, the maximum transient NR limit is 116%; 118% exceeds the permitted transient limit and is outside RFM limitations.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)

items.question: In power-off flight, what is the minimum transient NR allowed?
items.explanation: For power-off operation, the minimum transient NR is 90%; NR below this value is not permitted.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)

items.question: During autorotation, NR briefly drops to 90% before being restored. This is:
options: Within the minimum transient NR limit
Only allowed with all engines operating
items.explanation: For power-off operation, 90% NR is the minimum transient limit; it is only acceptable as a brief transient and not for sustained operation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ROTOR SPEED LIMITATIONS (Power-Off)

items.question: What is the minimum tail rotor gearbox (TGB) oil temperature for starting?
items.explanation: TGB oil temperature must be at or above -40 deg C for engine start.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TAIL ROTOR GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: During ground operation, TGB oil temperature is -10 deg C. This is:
options: Within the TGB ground operation range
Below the minimum ground operation limit
Above the maximum normal operation limit
items.explanation: For ground operation, TGB oil temperature is permitted between -40 deg C and 0 deg C; -10 deg C is within this range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TAIL ROTOR GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: Which TGB oil temperature range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal TGB oil temperature range in flight is from 1 deg C up to 110 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TAIL ROTOR GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: During flight, TGB oil temperature indicates 0 deg C. This is:
options: Below the normal range and only permitted on ground
items.explanation: 0 deg C is the upper limit of the ground operation range; normal in-flight TGB oil temperatures start at 1 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TAIL ROTOR GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the maximum normal TGB oil temperature limit?
items.explanation: The maximum normal TGB oil temperature is 110 deg C; temperatures above this value exceed the normal operating limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TAIL ROTOR GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: In cruise, TGB oil temperature rises to 115 deg C. This is:
options: Above the maximum normal temperature limit
items.explanation: Normal TGB oil temperature is limited to 110 deg C; 115 deg C exceeds the normal limit and requires corrective action.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TAIL ROTOR GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the minimum main gearbox (MGB) oil pressure at idle?
items.explanation: At idle, the minimum MGB oil pressure is 2.3 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MAIN GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: Which MGB oil pressure range is permitted at idle?
items.explanation: At idle, MGB oil pressure is allowed between 2.3 and 3.0 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MAIN GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the normal MGB oil pressure range in flight?
items.explanation: Normal MGB oil pressure in flight must be between 3.1 and 6.0 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MAIN GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: In cruise, MGB oil pressure stabilizes at 2.8 bar. This is:
options: Below the normal flight range and only acceptable at idle
items.explanation: Normal flight MGB oil pressure is 3.1 to 6.0 bar; 2.8 bar lies within the idle range and is abnormally low for cruise.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MAIN GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: In flight, MGB oil pressure indicates 6.2 bar. This is:
options: Above the maximum normal pressure limit
items.explanation: The normal MGB oil pressure range is up to 6.0 bar; 6.2 bar exceeds the maximum normal limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MAIN GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the maximum normal MGB oil pressure limit?
items.explanation: The upper limit of the normal MGB oil pressure range is 6.0 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MAIN GEARBOX LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the normal DC generator load range in percent?
items.explanation: Normal DC generator load is from 0% up to 100%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: During engine start, DC generator load briefly indicates 120%. This is:
options: Within the cautionary range for engine start only
items.explanation: Generator loads between 101% and 155% are allowed as a cautionary range during engine starting only.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: In cruise, DC generator load is stabilized at 120% on both generators. This is:
options: Above the normal range and only allowed during engine start
items.explanation: Generator loads above 100% are only permitted as a cautionary range during engine start; in flight this would exceed the normal operating limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the maximum DC generator cautionary load limit during engine start?
items.explanation: The cautionary generator load range during engine start extends up to a maximum of 155%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: Up to which altitude can the DC generators be operated at 100% (300 A) normal load?
items.explanation: Up to 15000 ft Hp, the DC generators may be operated at 100% normal load (300 A).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: At 20000 ft Hp, what is the maximum normal DC generator load?
items.explanation: At 20000 ft Hp, the maximum normal DC generator load is reduced to 33%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: With MPOG operating and generator load at 70%, what is the time limitation?
items.explanation: With MPOG and generator load up to and including 75%, there is no time limitation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: With MPOG operating and generator load at 90%, what is the time limitation?
items.explanation: With MPOG and generator load greater than 75%, operation is limited to 20 minutes.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the normal battery discharge current range?
items.explanation: Battery discharge is limited to the range -200 A to 0 A.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the normal main and essential bus voltage range?
items.explanation: The normal main and essential bus voltage range is 22 V to 29 V.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: With all engines operating, what is the maximum continuous Power Index (PI)?
items.explanation: For all engines operating, the maximum continuous PI is 100%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: With all engines operating, which PI range corresponds to Take-Off (5 minute) power?
items.explanation: Take-Off (5 minute) power with all engines operating corresponds to a PI range of 101% to 110%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: With all engines operating, what is the maximum PI allowed for Take-Off (5 minute) power?
items.explanation: For all engines operating, PI up to 110% is permitted for Take-Off power for a maximum of 5 minutes.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: With all engines operating, PI peaks at 115% for 4 seconds during take-off. This is:
items.explanation: PI values above 110% and up to 121% are permitted only as a 5-second transient; 115% for 4 seconds is within the transient limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: With all engines operating, what is the PI transient limit for 5 seconds?
items.explanation: For all engines operating, the PI transient limit is 121% for a maximum of 5 seconds.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: For one engine inoperative, what is the maximum continuous Power Index (PI)?
items.explanation: With one engine inoperative, the maximum continuous PI is 140%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: For one engine inoperative, which PI range corresponds to the 2.5 minute power rating?
items.explanation: For OEI, PI between 141% and 160% corresponds to the 2.5 minute power range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: During OEI climb, PI reaches 170% for 4 seconds. This is:
options: Within the OEI 2.5 minute PI range
Within the OEI 5-second transient PI limit
items.explanation: For OEI, PI up to 176% is permitted as a 5-second transient; 170% for 4 seconds is within the transient limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Index

items.question: With all engines operative, what is the maximum continuous transmission torque (TQ)?
items.explanation: For all engines operative, the maximum continuous torque is 100% TQ.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: With all engines operative, which torque range corresponds to Take-Off (5 minute) power?
items.explanation: For AEO operation, 101% to 110% TQ corresponds to Take-Off (5 minute) torque.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: During take-off with all engines operative, torque is held at 108% for 4 minutes. This is:
items.explanation: 108% TQ lies within the 101% to 110% Take-Off (5 minute) range and is acceptable for up to 5 minutes.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: During climb with all engines operative, torque is maintained at 115% for 4 minutes. This is:
options: Within the 5-second transient torque limit only
items.explanation: 115% TQ is above the 101% to 110% Take-Off range and is only permitted up to 121% as a 5-second transient.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: With all engines operative, what is the transmission torque transient limit for 5 seconds?
items.explanation: For AEO operation, torque up to 121% TQ is permitted as a 5-second transient limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: For one engine inoperative, what is the maximum continuous transmission torque?
items.explanation: In OEI operation, maximum continuous transmission torque is 140% TQ.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: For one engine inoperative, which torque range corresponds to the 2.5 minute power rating?
items.explanation: For OEI, 141% to 160% TQ corresponds to the 2.5 minute torque range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: During OEI climb, torque peaks at 170% for 4 seconds. This is:
options: Within the OEI 2.5 minute torque range
Within the OEI 5-second transient torque limit
items.explanation: For OEI, torque up to 176% TQ is permitted as a 5-second transient; 170% for 4 seconds is within this limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - Torque

items.question: What is the minimum Gas Generator Speed (NG) for ground idle?
items.explanation: The minimum NG for ground idle is 55.0%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: With all engines operating, which NG range is approved for continuous operation?
items.explanation: For AEO operation, continuous NG is between 55.1% and 100.0%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: During cruise with all engines operating, NG is stabilized at 99%. This is:
options: Within the transient NG range only
items.explanation: Continuous NG operation with all engines operating is allowed up to 100.0%; 99% is within the continuous range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: With all engines operating, which NG range corresponds to Take-Off (5 minute) power?
items.explanation: For AEO, NG between 100.1% and 102.4% corresponds to the 5-minute Take-Off range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: During take-off with all engines operating, NG peaks at 103% for 3 seconds. This is:
items.explanation: NG above 102.4% and up to 107.0% is permitted only as a 5-second transient; 103% for 3 seconds is within the transient limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: What is the NG transient limit (5 seconds) for both AEO and OEI operation?
items.explanation: For both AEO and OEI, the NG transient limit is 107.0% for a maximum of 5 seconds.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: For one engine inoperative, what is the maximum continuous NG?
items.explanation: In OEI operation, maximum continuous NG is 102.4%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: During OEI climb, NG is 105.5% for 2 minutes. This is:
options: Within the OEI 2.5 minute NG range
items.explanation: For OEI, NG from 102.5% to 106.0% is the 2.5 minute range; 105.5% for 2 minutes is within this range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - NG

items.question: What is the maximum unlimited ITT during engine start?
items.explanation: During engine start, ITT may be up to 869 deg C without a time limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT (Engine Starting)

items.question: During engine start, ITT peaks at 950 deg C for 1 second. This is:
items.explanation: An ITT up to 1000 deg C is permitted for a 2-second transient during engine start; 950 deg C for 1 second is within this transient limit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT (Engine Starting)

items.question: What is the ITT transient limit (2 seconds) during engine start?
items.explanation: During engine start, ITT may reach 1000 deg C for a maximum of 2 seconds.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT (Engine Starting)

items.question: With all engines operating, what is the maximum continuous ITT?
items.explanation: For AEO operation, maximum continuous ITT is 735 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT (All Engines Operating)

items.question: With all engines operating, which ITT range corresponds to Take-Off (5 minute) power?
items.explanation: For AEO, ITT between 736 deg C and 775 deg C corresponds to the 5-minute Take-Off range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT (All Engines Operating)

items.question: During take-off with all engines operating, ITT stabilizes at 780 deg C for 2 minutes. This is:
items.explanation: The Take-Off ITT range ends at 775 deg C; 780 deg C exceeds the Take-Off limit and is only permitted up to 847 deg C as a 5-second transient.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT (All Engines Operating)

items.question: What is the ITT transient limit (5 seconds) for AEO and OEI operation?
items.explanation: For both AEO and OEI, the ITT transient limit is 847 deg C for a maximum of 5 seconds.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT

items.question: For one engine inoperative, what is the maximum ITT for the 2.5 minute power rating?
items.explanation: In OEI operation, the 2.5 minute ITT range extends up to a maximum of 835 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - ITT (One Engine Inoperative)

items.question: What is the minimum engine oil temperature for engine starting?
items.explanation: Engine oil temperature must be at or above -40 deg C for engine start.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Engine Oil Temperature

items.question: During ground idle, engine oil temperature is 0 deg C. This is:
options: Within the ground idle cautionary range
items.explanation: For ground idle, engine oil temperature between -40 deg C and 9 deg C is a cautionary range; 0 deg C is within this range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Engine Oil Temperature

items.question: Which engine oil temperature range is considered normal operation in flight?
items.explanation: Normal engine oil temperature range is 10 deg C to 140 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Engine Oil Temperature

items.question: At torque below 60%, what is the maximum engine oil temperature permitted for up to 30 minutes?
items.explanation: For torque below 60%, engine oil temperature up to 145 deg C is permitted for a maximum of 30 minutes.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Engine Oil Temperature

items.question: What is the minimum engine oil pressure at ground idle (less than 1 minute)?
items.explanation: The minimum engine oil pressure at ground idle (less than 1 minute) is 4.2 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Engine Oil Pressure

items.question: Which engine oil pressure range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal engine oil pressure range is 6.3 to 8.9 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Engine Oil Pressure

items.question: Which sequence correctly describes the starter duty cycle?
options: 30 seconds on, 1 minute off, repeated indefinitely
45 seconds on, 1 minute off; 45 seconds on, 1 minute off; 45 seconds on, 30 minutes off
60 seconds on, 5 minutes off, repeated three times
45 seconds on, 5 minutes off, repeated twice
items.explanation: The approved starter duty cycle is: 45 s on, 1 min off; 45 s on, 1 min off; 45 s on, 30 min off.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Starter Duty Cycle

items.question: How often should engine power margin trend data be recorded for monitoring?
items.explanation: Engine power margin trend monitoring requires recording engine power assurance check values every 50 flight hours.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: POWER PLANT LIMITATIONS - Power Margin Trend Monitoring

items.question: What is the minimum main gearbox (MGB) oil temperature for starting?
items.explanation: MGB oil temperature must be at or above -40 deg C for starting.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Temperature

items.question: Which main gearbox (MGB) oil temperature range is approved for ground operation?
items.explanation: For MGB, the ground operation oil temperature range is -40 deg C to 0 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Temperature

items.question: Which main gearbox (MGB) oil temperature range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal MGB oil temperature range is 1 deg C to 110 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Temperature

items.question: What is the maximum normal main gearbox (MGB) oil temperature?
items.explanation: The maximum normal MGB oil temperature is 110 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Temperature

items.question: What is the minimum intermediate gearbox (IGB) oil temperature for starting?
items.explanation: IGB oil temperature must be at or above -40 deg C for starting.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - IGB Oil Temperature

items.question: Which intermediate gearbox (IGB) oil temperature range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal IGB oil temperature range is 1 deg C to 110 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - IGB Oil Temperature

items.question: What is the minimum tail rotor gearbox (TGB) oil temperature for starting?
items.explanation: TGB oil temperature must be at or above -40 deg C for starting.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - TGB Oil Temperature

items.question: Which tail rotor gearbox (TGB) oil temperature range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal TGB oil temperature range is 1 deg C to 110 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - TGB Oil Temperature

items.question: During ground operation, MGB oil temperature is -5 deg C. This is:
options: Within the MGB ground operation range
Below the minimum MGB start temperature
Above the maximum normal MGB temperature
items.explanation: The MGB ground operation range is -40 deg C to 0 deg C; -5 deg C is within this range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Temperature

items.question: What is the minimum main gearbox (MGB) oil pressure at idle?
items.explanation: The minimum MGB oil pressure at idle is 2.3 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Pressure

items.question: Which main gearbox (MGB) oil pressure range is permitted at idle?
items.explanation: At idle, MGB oil pressure must be between 2.3 and 3.0 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Pressure

items.question: Which main gearbox (MGB) oil pressure range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal MGB oil pressure range is 3.1 to 6.0 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Pressure

items.question: What is the maximum normal main gearbox (MGB) oil pressure?
items.explanation: The maximum normal MGB oil pressure is 6.0 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: TRANSMISSIONS LIMITATIONS - MGB Oil Pressure

items.question: What is the minimum hydraulic fluid temperature for flight control check with the electrical hydraulic pump?
items.explanation: For flight control checks using the electrical hydraulic pump, hydraulic fluid temperature must be at or above -50 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Temperature

items.question: What is the minimum hydraulic fluid temperature for starting?
items.explanation: Hydraulic fluid temperature must be at or above -40 deg C for starting.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Temperature

items.question: Which hydraulic fluid temperature range is approved for ground operation?
items.explanation: For the hydraulic system, the ground operation temperature range is -40 deg C to -21 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Temperature

items.question: What is the minimum hydraulic fluid temperature for normal operation?
items.explanation: The minimum hydraulic fluid temperature for normal operation is -20 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Temperature

items.question: Which hydraulic fluid temperature range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal hydraulic fluid temperature range is -20 deg C to 119 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Temperature

items.question: Which hydraulic fluid temperature range is cautionary?
items.explanation: Hydraulic fluid temperatures between 120 deg C and 134 deg C are in the cautionary range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Temperature

items.question: What is the minimum hydraulic fluid pressure in the cautionary low range?
items.explanation: The minimum cautionary hydraulic fluid pressure is 163 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Pressure

items.question: Which hydraulic fluid pressure range is considered normal operation?
items.explanation: Normal hydraulic fluid pressure range is 180 to 225 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Pressure

items.question: During operation, hydraulic pressure is 170 bar. This is:
options: Within the low cautionary pressure range
Within the high cautionary pressure range
items.explanation: 170 bar lies between 163 and 179 bar, which is the low cautionary hydraulic pressure range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Pressure

items.question: During operation, hydraulic pressure is 230 bar. This is:
options: Within the low cautionary pressure range
Within the high cautionary pressure range
items.explanation: 230 bar lies between 226 and 250 bar, which is the high cautionary hydraulic pressure range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Pressure

items.question: What is the maximum hydraulic fluid pressure in the cautionary range?
items.explanation: The maximum cautionary hydraulic fluid pressure is 250 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Hydraulic Fluid Pressure

items.question: For which phase of operation is the electrical hydraulic pump approved?
items.explanation: The electrical hydraulic pump is for ground operation only.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Electrical Hydraulic Pump

items.question: During cruise, you plan to use the electrical hydraulic pump as a backup with engines at idle. This plan is:
options: Approved, the electrical pump may be used in flight
Not approved, the electrical pump is for ground use only
items.explanation: The electrical hydraulic pump is limited to ground operation; its use in flight is not approved.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Electrical Hydraulic Pump

items.question: Which specification defines the authorized hydraulic fluids for the AW139 hydraulic system?
items.explanation: Authorized hydraulic fluids for the AW139 must comply with MIL-PRF-83282.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Authorized Hydraulic Fluids

items.question: What does the RFM state about mixing hydraulic fluids of different specifications?
options: It is permitted if the fluids have the same color
It is permitted for short periods only
It is permitted if noted in the maintenance log
items.explanation: The RFM explicitly states that mixing hydraulic fluid of different specifications is prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HYDRAULICS SYSTEM LIMITATIONS - Authorized Hydraulic Fluids

items.question: What is the maximum running speed for brake application?
items.explanation: Maximum running speed for brake application is 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WHEEL BRAKE LIMITATIONS

items.question: Parking on slopes up to 10 deg is permitted for a maximum of:
items.explanation: Parking on slopes up to 10 deg is permitted for a maximum of 1 hour.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WHEEL BRAKE LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the minimum AFCS configuration required for IFR flight?
items.explanation: The RFM states that the minimum AFCS configuration for IFR flight is 2 autopilots in ATT mode.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AUTOMATIC FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: During IFR flight, how is intentional ATT mode de-selection treated?
items.explanation: Intentional ATT MODE de-selection during IFR flight is prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AUTOMATIC FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS

items.question: For ILS glideslopes up to 4 degrees, what is the maximum airspeed?
items.explanation: For glideslopes up to 4 degrees, the maximum airspeed is 150 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ILS MODE LIMITATIONS

items.question: For steep ILS approaches with glideslopes between 4 and 7.5 degrees, what is the maximum airspeed?
items.explanation: For glideslopes between 4 and 7.5 degrees (steep approach), maximum airspeed is 120 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ILS MODE LIMITATIONS

items.question: During a steep ILS approach (4–7.5 deg glideslope), what is the correct use of Power Index (PI)?
options: Reduce PI to idle for a steeper descent
Maintain PI below 5% to avoid overspeed
PI limitations do not apply on ILS approaches
items.explanation: The RFM cautions that during steep approaches the pilot should take care not to use less than 5% PI.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: ILS MODE LIMITATIONS

items.question: Before flying an IFR procedure using the FMS, what must the pilot verify regarding the Navigation Data Base (NAV DB)?
options: Only that the NAV DB page opens
That the NAV DB is current and matches the intended procedure
That the NAV DB contains worldwide coverage
Only that the departure airport is present
items.explanation: The pilot must verify the currency of the NAV DB and the coherence of FMS data with the procedure to be flown.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FMS LIMITATIONS

items.question: When SBAS GPS is not installed or the aircraft is outside SBAS coverage, what FMS check is required before using GNSS for the approach?
options: Check predictive RAIM (P-RAIM) on the destination waypoint
items.explanation: When SBAS GPS is not available, predictive RAIM (P-RAIM) on the destination waypoint shall be checked on the MCDU.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FMS LIMITATIONS

items.question: Inside the Final Approach Fix (FAF), when is the pilot allowed to continue an instrument approach using the FMS?
options: Whenever lateral deviation is within one dot
Only when the ‘APP’ advisory is displayed on the PFD
Whenever the NAV DB procedure is selected
Only when both APs are engaged
items.explanation: The pilot must not continue an instrument approach inside the FAF unless the ‘APP’ advisory is displayed on the PFD.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FMS LIMITATIONS

items.question: Which type of non-precision approach is NOT authorised for use with the AW139 FMS?
items.explanation: Use of LDA, SDF and MLS approaches is not authorised by the FMS limitations.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: FMS LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the maximum baggage compartment load permitted?
items.explanation: Maximum baggage compartment load is 200 kg (440 lb) and all cargo must be properly secured.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIMITATIONS

items.question: What does the Height-Velocity diagram primarily define for the AW139?
options: Combinations of weight and temperature that limit take-off
Combinations of airspeed and height from which a safe single engine landing cannot be assured
Recommended climb speeds for one engine inoperative
items.explanation: The Height-Velocity diagram defines combinations of airspeed and height above ground from which a safe single engine landing on a smooth, level, hard surface cannot be assured in the event of a single engine failure.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: HEIGHT-VELOCITY LIMITATIONS

items.question: Under which conditions are Category A operations approved for the AW139?
items.explanation: The CAT A operations supplement states that Category A operations are approved under Day/Night conditions.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement: CAT A Operations - TYPES OF OPERATION

items.question: For a Category A take-off, what visual reference condition is required?
options: Visual references must exist only at the departure aerodrome
Visual references must exist in the FATO area and along the take-off distance
No visual references are required if IFR
Visual references are required only at the decision point
items.explanation: For CAT A take-off, weather conditions must be such that external visual references exist in the FATO area and in the take-off distance.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement: CAT A Operations - CATEGORY A TAKE OFF

items.question: For a Category A landing, where must visual references be available?
options: Only at the Final Approach Fix (FAF)
Only at the Landing Decision Point (LDP)
In the FATO area and in the balked landing area
Only at the helicopter landing gear
items.explanation: For CAT A landing, the approach to the LDP must be carried out with visual references in the FATO area and in the balked landing area.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement: CAT A Operations - CATEGORY A LANDING

items.question: When Category A take-off or landing is conducted from the left hand seat, what is the minimum flight crew requirement?
options: 1 pilot in the left hand seat
items.explanation: The supplement states that when CAT A take-off or landing is carried out from the left hand seat, minimum flight crew is 2 pilots.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement: CAT A Operations - CREW LIMITATIONS

items.question: How should the headwind component be applied when using the Category A W.A.T. charts for the AW139?
options: Apply the full headwind value as additional weight benefit
Apply no headwind benefit at all
Use the charts as published; the headwind gross weight benefit is already factored by 50%
Double the headwind value before entering the charts
items.explanation: The supplement states that the headwind gross weight benefit has already been factored by 50% into the W.A.T. charts and no further weight correction is necessary.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement: CAT A Operations - HEADWIND GROSS WEIGHT BENEFIT

items.question: During a power assurance check, one engine does not meet the required power check limits. What is the implication for Category A operations?
options: Category A operations may continue with reduced take-off weight
Category A operations are prohibited until engines meet power check requirements
Only night Category A operations are prohibited
Only training Category A operations are affected
items.explanation: The supplement states that Category A operations are prohibited if the engines do not meet the power check requirements.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement: CAT A Operations - POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS

items.question: You are planning a Category A Clear Area take-off with a forecast crosswind of 18 kts. What does the limitation require?
options: The take-off is permitted; the crosswind limit is 20 kts
The take-off is permitted if both autopilots are engaged
The take-off is not permitted because it exceeds the 15 kts crosswind limit for CAT A Clear Area procedures
The take-off is permitted only if the runway is dry
items.explanation: CATEGORY A WIND LIMITATIONS specify a maximum crosswind of 15 kts (8 m/s) for CAT A Clear Area Take Off and Landing.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: CATEGORY A WIND LIMITATIONS

items.question: What does the CATEGORY A WIND LIMITATIONS section state about take-off with a tailwind component?
options: Permitted if the surface is dry
items.explanation: The limitations clearly state that take-off with a tail wind component is prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: CATEGORY A WIND LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the limitation regarding the use of polarized type sun glasses by pilots?
options: They are recommended for glare reduction
They are permitted only in VMC
Pilots must not use polarized type sun glasses
They are permitted only for the pilot not flying
items.explanation: The miscellaneous limitations state that pilot(s) must not use polarized type sun glasses.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS

items.question: At MPOG/HIGE/HOGE or when helicopter forward velocity is below 25 kts, what ventilation action is required?
options: Operate the cockpit fans or open pilot/copilot window
items.explanation: The ventilation limitation states that at MPOG/HIGE/HOGE or at forward velocity below 25 kts, the cockpit fans shall be operated or the pilot/copilot window opened.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS - VENTILATION

items.question: If the TORQUE LIMITER is set, what is the maximum AEO torque available on the AW139?
items.explanation: The miscellaneous limitations specify that if the TORQUE LIMITER is set, maximum AEO torque available is 114%/114%.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS - TORQUE LIMITER FUNCTION

items.question: Following an MAU1 or MAU2 failure, how should the electrical and hydraulic synoptic MFD pages be used?
options: Use them as the primary reference
Use them only as backup to analog instruments
Do not refer to them because the information is not reliable
items.explanation: The synoptic MFD limitation states that in case of MAU1(2) failure, the electrical and hydraulic synoptic pages must not be used, as the information presented is not reliable.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS - SYNOPTIC MFD PAGE LIMITATION

items.question: What is the requirement for headset or helmet types used in the AW139 cockpit?
options: Headset/helmet type must be of the same electrical characteristics and authorised by the Aircraft Manufacturer
items.explanation: The miscellaneous limitations specify that headset/helmet type used in the aircraft must be of the same electrical characteristics and authorised by the Aircraft Manufacturer.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS - HEADSET/HELMET LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the maximum unit load allowed in the AW139 baggage compartment?
items.explanation: The baggage compartment limitations specify a maximum unit load of 300 kg/m2 (61 lb/sq ft).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIMITATIONS

items.question: Under normal operations, when is the rotor brake permitted to be actuated?
options: Whenever NR is below 60%, regardless of engine state
With at least one engine at ground idle
With at least one engine in flight mode
items.explanation: Rotor brake operation is limited to conditions with both engines OFF, as specified in the rotor brake limitations.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: What is the maximum rotor speed (NR) at which the rotor brake may be selected to BRAKE position during normal shutdown?
items.explanation: The rotor brake limitation specifies a maximum NR of 40% for selection to BRAKE position.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: When parking the AW139 using the rotor brake, what is the maximum time the rotor brake is considered effective in BRAKE position?
items.explanation: A note in the rotor brake limitations states that when in BRAKE position the rotor brake is effective for a maximum of 8 hours.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: What is the maximum permitted cargo height in the AW139 baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Baggage compartment limitations specify a maximum load height of 600 mm (2 ft).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIMITATIONS

items.question: During external hoist operations (Supplement 11), what is the maximum hoist load permitted?
items.explanation: The external hoist limitations specify a maximum hoist load of 272 kg (600 lb).
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: Within which pitch attitude range must the AW139 remain during hoist operations (Supplement 11)?
items.explanation: Hoist limitations specify that aircraft pitch angle during hoist operations must remain between -9 deg and +21 deg.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the maximum roll attitude permitted during hoist operations (Supplement 11)?
items.explanation: The hoist limitations specify a maximum roll angle of ±15 deg during hoist operations.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: What does the RFM state about take-off and landing with a suspended load on the hoist?
options: Permitted only in calm wind conditions
Prohibited; take-off and landing with a suspended hoist load are not allowed
items.explanation: Hoist limitations clearly state that take-off and landing with a suspended load on the hoist are prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: During hoist operations, how should the pilot use the AFCS/autopilot according to the limitations?
options: Operate fully coupled autopilot without additional monitoring
Fly manually or remain closely attentive when using the autopilot modes allowed by the supplement
Use autopilot only above 200 ft AGL
Engage all four autopilot channels for every hoist evolution
items.explanation: The hoist miscellaneous limitations state that during hoist operations the pilot must either fly manually or fly attentive when using the permitted autopilot modes.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the maximum load allowed on the AW139 cargo hook (Supplement 13)?
items.explanation: Cargo hook limitations specify a maximum load of 2200 kg (4850 lb) on the cargo hook.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 13: Cargo Hook Operations - CARGO HOOK LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the taxiing limitation for grass surfaces with the cargo hook extended?
options: Taxiing on grass surfaces with hook extended is permitted at low speed
Taxiing on grass surfaces with hook extended is permitted only with an empty hook
Taxiing on grass surfaces with hook extended is prohibited
Taxiing on grass surfaces with hook extended is permitted only in calm wind
items.explanation: The cargo hook limitations state that taxiing on grass surfaces with the hook extended is prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 13: Cargo Hook Operations - CARGO HOOK LIMITATIONS

items.question: How shall the pilot fly the AW139 during cargo hook operations according to the limitations?
options: With at least one autopilot channel engaged at all times
Manually; the pilot must fly the helicopter without relying on coupled autopilot modes for cargo hook manoeuvring
In heading hold and altitude hold modes only
items.explanation: The cargo hook miscellaneous limitations specify that during cargo hook operations the pilot must fly manually.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 13: Cargo Hook Operations - MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the limitation on using the Primus HF 1050 radio during cargo hook operations?
options: HF transmissions are permitted at reduced power only
HF transmissions are prohibited during cargo hook operations
HF may be used only above 3000 ft
HF may be used only in day VMC
items.explanation: The cargo hook miscellaneous limitations state that during cargo hook operations, Primus HF 1050 radio transmissions are prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 13: Cargo Hook Operations - MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS

items.question: How must the weather radar be configured during cargo hook operations?
options: May be used in any mode
Must be in STBY or OFF
May be used in MAP mode only
items.explanation: Cargo hook miscellaneous limitations require that during cargo hook operations the weather radar be in standby (STBY) or OFF.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 13: Cargo Hook Operations - MISCELLANEOUS LIMITATIONS

items.question: When setting the rotor brake lever to BRAKE position for parking, what is the minimum brake system pressure that should initially be achieved?
items.explanation: Rotor brake limitations specify a minimum pressure of 40 BAR for the lever in BRAKE position; after up to 8 hours a lower pressure is acceptable, but the initial setting should be at least 40 BAR.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: What is the maximum rotor brake pressure allowed when the lever is in BRAKE position?
items.explanation: Rotor brake limitations specify that when the lever is in BRAKE position the pressure must not exceed 62.5 BAR.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: After parking with the rotor brake in BRAKE position for up to 8 hours, what is the minimum acceptable brake system pressure?
items.explanation: The rotor brake limitations state that after a maximum of 8 hours in BRAKE position the minimum acceptable pressure is 26 BAR.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: Under which condition is an emergency rotor brake application from approximately 90% NR permitted?
options: Only to prevent overrun on a short stand
Only in an emergency situation as specified in the RFM
During training to verify rotor brake capability
items.explanation: The rotor brake limitations allow an emergency application from about 90% NR only in an emergency situation.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: What is the correct rotor brake lever position for engine start on the AW139?
options: BRAKE position to prevent rotor spin
Any position as long as NR is zero
OFF position; engine start with rotor brake applied is prohibited
BRAKE position until 20% NR then OFF
items.explanation: Rotor brake limitations require the rotor brake lever to be in OFF position for engine starting; starting with the brake applied is prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 1: ROTOR BRAKE - Limitations

items.question: During external hoist operations (Supplement 11), what is the maximum forward airspeed permitted?
items.explanation: Hoist limitations permit external hoist operations in stationary hover and in forward flight up to 80 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: According to the hoist limitations (Supplement 11), what are the two possible maximum hoist cable lengths depending on the installed hoist part number?
items.explanation: The hoist limitations specify that maximum hoist cable length is either 75 m or 90 m depending on the hoist part number installed.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: For which flight regimes are external hoist operations authorised on the AW139 according to the limitations?
options: In stationary hover and in forward flight up to the specified airspeed limit
In any flight regime including autorotation
items.explanation: The hoist limitations authorise operations in stationary hover and in forward flight up to the published speed limit; other regimes such as autorotation are not intended for hoist work.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 11: External Hoist Operations - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: For the double external hoist installation (Supplement 41), what is the maximum hoist load permitted when OAT is above 0 deg C?
items.explanation: The double hoist limitations specify a maximum hoist load of 550 lb (249 kg) when OAT is above 0 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 41: Double External Hoist - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: For the double external hoist installation, what is the maximum hoist load permitted when OAT is at or below 0 deg C?
items.explanation: The double hoist limitations reduce the maximum hoist load to 500 lb (227 kg) when OAT is at or below 0 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 41: Double External Hoist - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: For the double external hoist installation, what is the maximum allowable load on the boom?
items.explanation: The double hoist limitations specify a maximum load on the boom of 272 kg (600 lb).
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 41: Double External Hoist - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: With the double external hoist installation and cable extended, what is the maximum bank angle permitted?
items.explanation: The double hoist limitations specify a maximum permissible bank angle of 20 deg with the cable extended.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 41: Double External Hoist - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: What lateral pendulum angle of the suspended load is highlighted as critical in the double hoist limitations due to possible clutch slippage?
items.explanation: A warning in the double hoist limitations notes that exceeding about 15 deg lateral pendulum angle may lead to hoist clutch slippage.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 41: Double External Hoist - HOIST LIMITATIONS

items.question: For dual cargo hook operations (Supplement 98), what is the maximum total external load allowed?
items.explanation: Dual cargo hook limitations specify a maximum total load of 800 kg (1766 lb) for dual hook operation.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 98: Dual Cargo Hook System - LIMITATIONS

items.question: What is the taxiing limitation for dual cargo hook operations with hooks extended?
options: Taxiing on any surface is permitted at low speed
Taxiing on unprepared surfaces with hooks extended is prohibited
Taxiing on paved surfaces is prohibited
Taxiing is permitted only with empty hooks
items.explanation: The dual cargo hook limitations state that taxiing on unprepared surfaces with the hooks extended is prohibited.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 98: Dual Cargo Hook System - LIMITATIONS

items.question: According to the dual cargo hook system limitations, when should PCDS releases normally be completed?
options: In flight to reduce landing weight
On the ground only, unless required in an emergency
items.explanation: Dual cargo hook limitations specify that PCDS releases are to be completed on the ground only, except when an in-flight release is required in an emergency.
references: AW139 RFM Supplement 98: Dual Cargo Hook System - LIMITATIONS
